title: Homeware retailer: a shorter returns window
question: What could happen if a homeware retailer shortens its returns window from 60 days to 30 days?

documents.name: 01-policy-proposal.md
documents.content:
# Policy proposal: a shorter returns window

This is a fictional proposal written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Proposal

Brindle & Hart, a homeware retailer with 41 shops and an online store, proposes to shorten its returns window from 60 days to 30 days. Returns of items bought in the sale would stay at 14 days.

## Reason

The retailer says that returns cost it about 8% of annual sales through handling, damage and resale at a discount. The finance lead expects a shorter window to cut returns by a fifth. The online store manager notes that most returns arrive in the last two weeks of the window.

## Timing

The change would be announced in the January newsletter and take effect on 1 March.

documents.name: 02-customer-and-service-data.md
documents.content:
# Customer and service data

This is a fictional summary written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Returns

The customer service team reports that returns cost the retailer about 12% of annual sales. Of returned items, 35% are resold at full price and 40% are resold at a discount.

## Contacts

Calls to the contact centre about returns rise sharply in the last week of the window. Customers who buy furniture online say they need time to assemble and live with an item before deciding.

## Feedback

A survey of 900 customers found that 64% say the returns window affects whether they buy bigger items. Customers who buy gifts in December often receive them after the 30-day point.

documents.name: 03-legal-and-logistics-note.md
documents.content:
# Legal and logistics note

This is a fictional note written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Consumer rights

The Marden Consumer Code gives online buyers a right to cancel within 14 days of delivery. It does not apply to goods bought in a shop. The code says that a seller must state its returns terms clearly before purchase and must not change them for orders already placed.

## Stores and warehouse

The warehouse handles returned online orders and is at capacity in January and February. Shop managers say that shop returns are done at the till and need no extra space. The carrier collects returns for a fee that rises in peak weeks.

## Partners

Two marketplaces that sell the retailer's goods set their own returns rules, which the retailer cannot change.
